subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: sharing prompts and lessons in a team log [Action]
passage: Sit down, Yusuf. You asked how our team got good with these AI tools. Honestly, it wasn't the clever ones among us. When we started, three people knew the tricks and everyone else kept guessing. So I began a shared page. Whenever someone found a request that worked, they pasted it in with one line on why; whenever one failed, they pasted that too, and what went wrong. Every Friday afternoon, before chai, we read the page together for twenty minutes. Nobody was laughed at for a failure. Within two months, people who hadn't dared before were adding entries, and the same mistake stopped repeating. I'm Harish, and if you take one thing from me: skill kept in one head leaves when that person does.

qa.q: When did the team read the shared page together?
qa.a: They read it every Friday afternoon, before chai, for twenty minutes.

qa.q: What did Harish want when starting the shared page?
qa.a: Harish wanted skill to spread across the team instead of staying with three people, worried that it would leave with them.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story helped quiet members start adding entries, and why?
qa.a: Not laughing at failures helped, since it made it safe for people who had not dared before to share what went wrong.

qa.q: How might a quiet team member have felt before the page existed?
qa.a: They were probably unsure and a little left out, guessing while three colleagues seemed to know the tricks.

grounding: Shows team members noting prompts that worked and failed and reviewing them on Fridays so skill grows across the team.
